publicBrief.acceptedPolicy: A download must pass the owner-aware view_document check on the root document before serving any selected file version.
publicBrief.currentQuestion: At DocumentViewSet.download handler entry, can an authenticated user download a requested version document they own when its root document is owned by someone else and they lack an object view grant on that root? Assume the user has the required global view permission and the documents exist.
premises: At download entry, the authenticated caller has global document view permission and owns the requested version, but a different user owns the existing root document and the caller has no object view grant on that root.
requiredResponseDetails: Identify which object is checked and which file object would be served; do not collapse version ownership into root authorization.

results.explanation: At the declared entry, the supplied source shows that DocumentViewSet.download receives a request and version/document identifier pk, then delegates to file_response(pk, request, "attachment"). The supplied crop does not show which object file_response binds to, whether it checks the root document, whether it applies an owner-aware view_document authorization check, or which file object is ultimately served. Therefore the source-visible behavior at this boundary is unknown, and the accepted root-view policy cannot be proved satisfied or violated from the supplied source alone. The current premises identify the caller as an authenticated user with global view permission who owns the requested version but lacks view access to the separately owned root; those premises are assumptions, not source citations. The decisive missing fact is the source-visible implementation and binding path of file_response, including the root authorization check and selected-version file effect. This does not establish repository-wide completeness because source discovery is not-tested.
